entities.summary:
En-hegal, possibly a ruler of the Sumerian city-state of Lagash, is known from the 'Tablet of En-hegal', which describes a business transaction.

As a ruler, En-hegal's existence is confirmed by the inscription, which is the only documented evidence of his reign.

The inscription provides a unique window into the administrative and economic systems of ancient Sumer.

En-hegal's significance lies in the fact that it is one of the earliest known examples of a ruler's personal involvement in the daily life of a city-state.
